startup.name: Revnu
startup.description: Revnu is an AI growth hire for founders. It connects to a company's tools, researches buyers, prepares outreach, runs paid ads and publishes search content, then measures results and applies what it learns across channels. The founder approves only the work that needs judgment and receives a morning digest. Customers are small founder-led software and service companies that pay a monthly fee in place of a growth hire or agency. Three founders in Manchester, UK.

yc_acceptance.basis: In this test the company is assumed accepted to YC for the Spring 2026 batch, so the acceptance estimate is a placeholder note. The prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent, references/yc_acceptance.md). A three person technical team in the hottest category (AI agents) with a clear paid job would sit above that, but the idea is copyable and crowded, so roughly 2 to 3 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because AI growth agents are a very crowded category with several funded entrants, the pitch has no stated traction, and a general purpose agent could copy the workflow. Interviewers would ask why this team wins distribution against better funded tools and whether founders will really pay for autonomous output.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: seed 49/59/65 (cond 59%, n=126), series_a 13/15/29 (cond 26%, n=74), series_b 2/2/18 (cond 16%, n=19), series_c 0/0/16 (cond 0%, n=3). The 2022+ rows are right censored; the older B2B 2018-2021 cohort gives cond A 32% (n=56), B 39% (n=18), C 57% (n=7).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Slightly below the 59 percent B2B 2022+ anchor (0.88x): the category is crowded and the stated deal is only about 12 months to a round above the YC check, while median time to seed is 7 months (p75 15), so a part of the 59 percent arrives later than the window.

bands.rationale: Small pre-seed above the standard YC deal from AI-focused angels and micro funds, the most common outcome for a three person AI tools team; ties to the 2022+ B2B p25 of 1.9M.
Typical seed near the 2022+ B2B median of 3.2M and the market median pre money near 18M cited in stage_benchmarks.md.
Hot AI seed if usage grows quickly after Demo Day; AI tag seeds in the cohort reach the 75th percentile of 5M or more.

ladder.why_it_fails: Growth agents show visible output but investors want proof of revenue retention, and founder-run companies churn quickly when the AI output needs heavy editing. With Hyperdesk, Gooseworks and Sprites all pitching similar marketing agents and no funding recorded for most of them, investors may judge this a feature war and stay at the YC check, leaving the company without a round above 500K inside a year.

ladder.why_it_fails: Few small business marketing tools reach a Series C because the customer base is price sensitive and large platforms add the same features, so growth slows at around tens of millions of revenue and the company is usually acquired, as many YC marketing software companies such as Positional have been.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in a small sale or a stall because AI marketing agents are close to commodity features that platforms and general agents can replicate, small business customers churn quickly, and YC marketing software analogs such as Positional and RankScience ended in modest acquisitions or small businesses.

killers.risk: Crowded category and copyable by general agents or CRM suites
killers.evidence: Many funded and YC companies sell AI marketing agents, and the competition search shows Salesforce and HubSpot offering similar agents.
killers.mitigation: Win a narrow customer, such as one vertical of technical founders, and own the data loop that improves results.

killers.risk: Output quality does not beat a human marketer, so customers churn
killers.evidence: Autonomous ad and outreach output often needs heavy edits; cold outreach also faces deliverability limits.
killers.mitigation: Report revenue attribution per approval and offer pricing tied to results.

killers.risk: Seed round never exceeds the YC check because investors see a feature, not a company
killers.evidence: Several similar marketing agent companies in the YC data have no round recorded.
killers.mitigation: Show paying customers with retention at Demo Day.

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting many marketing channels and learning across them is integration heavy but a three person team can ship a version in months using model APIs. The hard part is attribution and quality of output, not model research.

who: general coding and computer use agents
takeover_risk.rationale: A rival with distribution could assemble the same agent workflow in under a year, and incumbents already ship similar agents. Customers' ad and CRM accounts are controlled by the platforms.

evidence.claim: Marketing teams already buy and compare many AI marketing agent products, showing spend, though vendor lists are self interested.
Dozens of competing AI growth agent tools are listed on comparison sites, showing crowded demand.

actions: Interview 30 founders who do no growth work
Run the agent manually for 5 paying customers

roadmap.proof: Net revenue retention above 100 percent on 20 customers

pros.point: Clear paid job: replace a growth hire founders cannot afford
pros.evidence: Founders without a marketer are a defined buyer and agencies cost more.

pros.point: Hot category with active seed investor interest
pros.evidence: Comparable AI agent companies in the YC data reach seed at higher rates than the 59 percent anchor.

brand.name: Revnu
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Revnu" --era 2022+ : 5 characters, 2 syllables, invented, no suffix
brand.strengths: Short and easy to type, signals revenue
brand.weaknesses: Clipped spelling is hard to say and easy to misspell; the vowel drop is a common 2020s pattern
brand.rationale: The name is short and hints at revenue, which matches the job. The dropped vowel makes it harder to find by ear, but past YC names with this style rarely failed because of the name, so the effect is small.

narrative.headline: Plausible early seed for a crowded AI growth agent, with a hard path to a venture scale Series A.
narrative.general_summary: Revnu sells an AI growth hire to founders, a useful job in a very crowded and copyable category. The team is three people with no stated traction in the description. Past YC marketing agents show few rounds beyond a small seed and incumbents are adding the same agents. The seed over 500K within a year is a bit under a coin flip and later steps follow the base rates, with the upside path coming from a pivot to a narrower customer or a deeper analytics layer.

assumptions: Test is blind: only the YC input file was used for company facts.
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months of the batch start.
Cohort data for 2022+ is right censored.
